cluster_summary: A collection of vulnerabilities where protocol parsers (HTTP, email, AJP, etc.) fail to validate user-supplied input for control characters, enforce protocol-specific constraints, or limit resource consumption, leading to CRLF injection, request smuggling, denial of service, or email header manipulation.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata into memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work. Report code paths where protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 7 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work.

mechanism.missing_guard: protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion
mechanism.name: unbounded binary length or size field drives resource use
mechanism.sink_shape: memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Introduce configurable limits (e.g., maxFields, maxBytes, maxHeaders), use efficient algorithms (e.g., O(n log n) sort), and track cumulative sizes incrementally to prevent resource exhaustion.
sub_patterns.name: Resource exhaustion due to missing limits in input parsing
sub_patterns.root_cause: The parser does not impose limits on the number of fields, field sizes, buffer sizes, or algorithmic complexity, allowing an attacker to cause unbounded memory or CPU consumption.
